newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end higher to up $10.00 limit.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end higher to up $10.00 limit.

text.p: CME lumber futures finished higher to up as much as the daily $10.00 per tbf daily limit after starting lower and then rallying on short covering from technicals and stronger-than-expected fundamentals, traders said.
November and January closed limit up with November at $350.90 per tbf and January at $359.70. Other months ended up $9.30 to $6.00 with May setting a new high of $367.00.

Futures again held technical support on the early decline and rallied on short covering with buy stops hit above $347.00 per tbf, basis November. Talk of firmer cash lumber prices added to the late gain bolstered values up the limit, traders said.

"It' a technical rally after a considerable retracement of the September move, said Tim Elrod, lumber trader for Pacific Futures Trading. Elrod also said he looks for November futures to go back up to $430 per tbf on both technical and fundamental factors. The Canadian goverment is restricting exports and lumber supplies are tightening due to its 90-year crop cycle, he said.
"I expect by spring this (cash) lumber market to be over $600 on big demand and no supply," Elrod said.
